To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

foot agility, toe graphaesthesia, and toe gnosis are sensitive to the integrity of the medial surfaces (especially the dorsal half) of the cerebral hemi spheres, and that these three measures are useful indicators of the functional status of this region of the brain.

deficits for foot agility and toe graphaesthesiawere more consistently correlated with general measures of brain impairment and with cognitive tests whose normal performance requires intact structures within the dorsal medial cerebral hemispheric surface, and that deficits for toe gnosis were more consistently correlated with tests whose normal performance is dependent on the ventral medial hemispheric surface.

the performance on tests for foot agility and toe gnosis and graphaesthesia is a function of the integrity of the medial surfaces, particularly the dorsal surface of the cerebral hemi-spheres, in the normal population and in clinical populations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of potential indicators of the integrity of the medial cerebral surfaces, with the hope that such indicators will be useful for the identification of patients with closed-head injury who are at risk for developing cognitive impairments.
developing a new set of quantitative indicators that can help us understand the integrity of the medial cerebral surface.
the development of a quantitative assessment procedure for the integrity of medial cerebral structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
toe graphaesthesia is a reliable, valid, and sensitive indicator of the integrity of the medial cerebral surface.
toe graphaesthesia is a reliable and sensitive indicator of the integrity of the dorsal medial cerebral hemispheric surfaces.
foot agility and toe gnosis are sensitive to damage to the dorsal medial surface of the cerebral hemispsheres.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the integrity of the medial cerebral surfaces can be quantitatively assessed by the performance of tasks that require the ability to identify the location of a touch on the toes (toe gnosis) and to discriminate between the location of a light touch on two adjacent toes (toe graphaesthesia).
the integrity of the medial surface of the cerebral hemi-spheres can be assessed with the use of quantitative indicators of function.

the medial cerebral surface can be probed by the use of foot and toe tasks, that these tasks can be administered in a reliable manner, that they have the potential for use as indicators of brain integrity, and that the most sensitive indicator is toe graphaesthesia, especially in patients with closed-head injuries.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the integrity of the medial cerebral surface can be assessed with quantitative measures of foot agility, toe graphaesthesia, and toe gnosis, with deficits for the latter two being more consistently correlated with general measures of brain impairment.
toe graphaesthesia is a sensitive indicator of the integrity of the medial cerebral surface, particularly the dorsomedial frontal and parietal cortices.
the foot and toes are a rich source of information regarding the integrity and functioning of the brain, and the use of the foot and toes in clinical neuropsychology should be more widely explored.
